cohort: 5200 pregnant Thai women who delivered at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Faculty of Medicine Siriraj Hospital between September 1, 2011 and August 1, 2012
finding: The study proposed optimal gestational weight gain ranges for each pre-pregnancy BMI group, finding that adhering to these recommendations was associated with a higher proportion of appropriate-for-gestational-age infants and decreased adverse pregnancy outcomes.
mod_finding: The study found that cesarean section rates were lower in women who adhered to the proposed gestational weight gain recommendations.
